Resolves #18931

A build script reached through a symlinked path runs its CLI block again, instead of exiting 0 having checked nothing. Every entry check in `buildScripts/` and `test/playwright/` now asks `buildScripts/util/isEntryModule.mjs`. The helper realpaths `process.argv[1]` and the module's own URL alike, which is the pattern the published neo-agent-skills guards use. `check-class-module-scope`'s comment, which called the old `path.resolve` form symlink-safe, goes with it.

Evidence: **L2** — the helper's spec, including a real guard run through a symlinked checkout that is red on `dev`, plus every migrated CLI exercised by hand and six of them by this commit's own hook. Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline jobs ran. Change class: `defect` (`fix`).

## AC Evidence

| AC | |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `unit/buildScripts/util/isEntryModule.spec.mjs` › "the script node runs is the entry: through its real path, a symlinked one, and --preserve-symlinks-main", and › "an imported module is not the entry, and nothing is when argv names no script on disk" |
| AC-2 | same spec › "a guard run through a symlinked checkout path reports instead of exiting silently" runs `check-guard-ci-parity.mjs` through a symlink to the repo. With `dev`'s copy of that guard the arm fails, because the guard prints nothing |
| AC-3 | `git grep -n 'process.argv\[1\]' -- buildScripts test/playwright` finds the helper's comment in `check-class-module-scope.mjs`, specs, and `check-secrets.mjs`, which retires in #18929 and is excluded by the ticket |

## Deltas from ticket

- **The `endsWith('<name>.mjs')` checks migrated too** (`check-spec-retirement`, `e2eCiSelection`, `flickerCensus`). They survive a symlink, but a single rule is easier to hold than an exception. `git grep` now answers "who compares `argv[1]` by hand" with nothing.
- **Imports the check was the last user of are gone**: `fileURLToPath` or `pathToFileURL` in 11 files, and `path` plus a `__filename` in `agent-push.mjs`. The hook's `check-block-alignment --fix` realigned the import blocks that shortened. It also fixed alignment drift already on `dev` in `check-relative-links` (its `let` block) and `check-theme-surfaces` (one object literal).
- **`check-class-module-scope.spec.mjs` follows the guard.** Its real-guard arm copies `isEntryModule.mjs` beside the copied guard and reverts the new line. Its probe arm checks the helper against a space-containing path instead of an inline copy of the old expression.

## Test Evidence

- Mutations: `isEntryModule` comparing `argv[1]` unresolved fails the symlinked-path assertion and the real-guard arm. `dev`'s `check-guard-ci-parity.mjs` fails the real-guard arm (`Expected: not ""`).
- The migrated CLIs run their blocks: `e2eCiSelection` (46 bytes of output), `static-closure --list src/Neo.mjs` (225), `check-package-contents` (205), and `check-codeql-extraction --help` (exit 2, its usage path). The commit's hook ran `check-secrets`, `check-guard-ci-parity`, `check-derived-domain`, `check-jsdoc-types`, `check-fixed-sleeps` and `check-engine-brain-boundary` through the new check, all green.
- Unit: full tier 4294 passed, 2 skipped; `unit/buildScripts` 793. Components `form`: 27, through the webServer step that runs `globalSetup.mjs` first.

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

Per §9 Strategic-Fit Step-Back:
- **Decision**: Approve
- **Rationale**: 33 hand-rolled copies of one predicate become one helper, and the predicate was *wrong* in every copy. A migration this wide earns its blast radius only if the new single answer is provably right and the old sites are provably gone — both are demonstrated here rather than asserted.

**Peer-Review Opening:** The failure mode is the nastiest kind: the script exits **0** having checked nothing. A guard that fails loudly gets fixed the first time it runs; this one reports success while doing nothing, which is why it survived across 33 files.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — the helper's `catch` recreates the bug it fixes, in miniature.**

```js
try {
    return realpathSync(entry) === realpathSync(fileURLToPath(importMetaUrl))
} catch {
    return false
}
```

`false` is the right default — throwing would break every script, and `true` would run CLI blocks on import — so this is not a wrong choice. But the catch is total, and the consequence of a non-`ENOENT` throw (`ELOOP` on a symlink cycle, a permissions error on a mounted checkout) is precisely the symptom of #18931: **the script exits 0 having checked nothing**, and nobody learns. It is a small surface — `argv[1]` exists because node resolved it, and the module URL exists because it is executing — so I would not block on it. Worth considering whether a non-`ENOENT` error deserves a `console.warn` before returning false, so the one case that reaches here is not silent. Your call; the documented `@returns` already tells the truth about the `false`.

**What I actively looked for and did not find:**

- **An incomplete migration.** I re-ran AC-3's grep at this head rather than reading the claim. The survivors are exactly what it says: the helper's own comment and body, `check-class-module-scope.mjs:250`'s comment, spec fixtures that deliberately embed the fragile expression as test data, and `check-secrets.mjs:143` — which #18934 deletes, and which I confirmed is excluded by the ticket rather than overlooked.
- **A migration that changed behaviour.** Spot-checked both shapes. `watchThemes.mjs` moves from `pathToFileURL(path.resolve(argv[1]))` — equivalent-when-unsymlinked, so a pure strengthening. `check-spec-retirement.mjs` moves from `endsWith('check-spec-retirement.mjs')`, which was not merely symlink-fragile but **loose**: it matches any path ending in that basename, including a *copy* of the guard at another location — which is exactly what the real-guard spec arms construct. Your Deltas call the `endsWith` migration a consistency choice; it is also a correctness one.
- **A helper with only negative coverage.** The spec runs three positives (real path, symlinked, `--preserve-symlinks-main`) and two negatives (imported module, `argv[1]` naming nothing). Both directions, which is what stops the "returns false for everything" regression from passing.

**On AC-2 specifically:** running `check-guard-ci-parity.mjs` through a symlink to the repo and asserting it *reports* — red on `dev` because the guard prints nothing — is the right witness. Asserting the exit code alone would have passed on `dev`, since exiting 0 having checked nothing is what the bug does.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit (per guide §7.4):**

- [x] PR description: framing matches the diff, including the honest note that `check-block-alignment --fix` also repaired pre-existing drift in two files it touched for other reasons.
- [x] Anchor & Echo: the helper's module docblock explains the *mechanism* (node resolves symlinks in the entry module's URL, never in `argv[1]`) rather than restating the rule. Retiring `check-class-module-scope`'s comment that called the old form symlink-safe is the right companion edit — a stale comment asserting the opposite of the new truth is worse than none.
- [x] Linked anchors: #18929's exclusion checks out.
